claim: Generalization from synthetic to real-world tasks via post-training alignment is most successful when the target task is structurally similar to the synthetic tasks used during alignment.
falsifier: For a set of real-world tasks with varying structural similarity to the synthetic training tasks, measure post-alignment performance gains; gains should be largest for tasks most similar to the synthetic task structure.

conditions: post-training alignment performed on synthetic data
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported synthetic task families, real-world benchmarks, and alignment settings; transfer beyond them is unestablished.
